project: ML-Based Thermal Risk Prediction in a Multi-Sensor Thermal System

key_metrics.metric: Rows with all three risk targets

assumption_evidence.evidence: 53,061 of 53,075 physical rows were structurally complete (99.9736% retention); rejected rows were reported.
Explicit ERR explains 1,456 of 1,462 missing sensor readings (99.59%).
Estimable sequence intervals range from 16.32 to 16.44 seconds; nine sequences prevent cross-gap windows.
NORMAL represents 5m=92.56%, 10m=88.59%, 15m=85.04%; accuracy therefore overstates minority-class performance.
Median slope by 15-minute risk: LOW=-0.0000, NORMAL=-0.0000, HIGH=0.0039 °C/min.
All 14 absolute-temperature columns changed by exactly +0.2 °C; slopes, spread, and labels remained unchanged.
Validation balanced accuracy across 5/10/15 minutes was 0.653/0.628/0.627, the strongest model-wise result at each horizon.
All 5 leakage/reproducibility checks passed; sequences 8 and 9 are absent from training and validation.
Final HIGH recall across 5/10/15 minutes is 0.365/0.465/0.466; minority-risk detection remains moderate.

leakage_audit.audit: Future values and targets excluded from model features
Train and validation sequences are disjoint
Test sequences are absent from final model training
All three targets exist in the Stage 3 dataset
Saved feature count matches feature list

plots.title: Stage 1 data retention
plots.evidence: Supports the decision to exclude only structurally invalid records after reporting them, while retaining 53,061 of 53,075 rows.

plots.title: Sensor-quality evidence
plots.evidence: Supports preserving ERR flags and missing values rather than silently imputing them during data preparation.

plots.title: Continuous sequences and sampling
plots.evidence: Supports reconstructing time within sequences and forbidding history or targets from crossing gaps and backward timestamps.

plots.title: Target availability and risk-class balance
plots.evidence: Supports multi-horizon modeling and the use of balanced metrics rather than accuracy alone.

plots.title: Historical-feature availability
plots.evidence: Confirms that missing values at sequence starts grow with the window length, as required by leakage-safe history construction.

plots.title: Temperature slope by future risk
plots.evidence: Directly tests the decision to add 5-, 10-, and 15-minute slope features. The plot shows association, not causation.

plots.title: Current features by 15-minute risk
plots.evidence: Examines the practical decision to include duty_pct and sensor_spread_c alongside active-sensor temperatures.

plots.title: Class distribution by chronological split
plots.evidence: Shows the distribution shift between Train, Validation, and HATCH-only Test data, explaining why accuracy alone is not sufficient.

plots.title: HATCH normalization verification
plots.evidence: Confirms that only absolute temperatures moved by +0.2 °C while slopes, spread, identifiers, and risk labels remained unchanged.

plots.title: Validation model comparison
plots.evidence: Supports selecting the tuned Random Forest using balanced accuracy under severe class imbalance, while retaining accuracy and macro F1.

plots.title: Final test performance
plots.evidence: Shows useful overall prediction performance while making the moderate HIGH recall and horizon-dependent degradation explicit.
